# Account-level proof: blast radius and early warning by npm account

**Question.** Is "which accounts can publish what we depend on" worth building on? Three claims were
tested on recorded real data, replayed offline. The methods and pass/fail rules were committed in
[PREREGISTRATION.md](../blastradius/test/replay/account/PREREGISTRATION.md) before any number was computed.

## Verdict

| Claim | Result | In one line |
|---|---|---|
| **H1** compromise response | **holds for a multi-package takeover (chalk/debug), weak for Shai-Hulud, nothing for event-stream** | When debug's advisory appeared, only 1 advisory existed. "qix is compromised" named all 19 bad packages at once, 2.7 h (median) and up to 6.4 h before their own advisories. In the org it named 204 package-level exposures instead of 21, and all 21 locked bad versions instead of 1. |
| **H2** burst early warning | **fails as an alert** | The rule fires before the advisory for qix (1.1 h) and for all 25 Shai-Hulud accounts with ≥5 attributable bad packages (0.2–45 h). But normal accounts burst about **2.1 times per account-month**, or 1.1 without bots. The pre-registered limit was 0.1. sindresorhus alone has 11 episodes in 7 months and isaacs 8. The 24 h variant gives 2.0. N≥10 gives 1.7 and misses qix. |
| **H3** concentration | descriptive | Each project depends on 45–234 publishing accounts. The top account can publish 9–27% of its packages (sindresorhus, ljharb or jonschlinkert in most projects; microsoft1es and "GitHub Actions" trusted publishing in TypeScript and mocha). |

**What this means for the product.** The account index and the "account X is compromised" query
earn their place. They turn the first advisory of a multi-package takeover into a complete answer
hours before the per-package advisories finish, and they need no re-scan. The burst rule does not
earn a standalone alert: routine monorepo and prolific-maintainer releases look the same as a worm.
At most it is a low-weight input to combine with other signals, which was not tested here.

**Follow-up (2026-10-08):** a pre-registered zero-shot Laya triage step on each burst was tested in
[LAYA-TRIAGE.md](LAYA-TRIAGE.md). It fails: 0.427 false alarms per test-control account-month, and
only 13 of 25 Shai-Hulud early warnings kept.

## Caveats (read before quoting the numbers)

- **Deleted versions lose their publisher.** npm removed the bad versions; their `_npmUser` is gone.
  A publisher is attributed only when the previous version had a single maintainer. That leaves
  389/589 wave-1 and 682/1,122 wave-2 Shai-Hulud bad versions unattributed (excluded, not guessed).
  For qix, 15 of 19 bad publishes are attributable. The Shai-Hulud accounts analysed are therefore
  the sole-maintainer subset, and H2 incident catches are a lower bound on what a live watcher
  (which sees `_npmUser` before deletion) would get.
- **"Can publish at T"** comes from the `maintainers` recorded on the latest version at or before T.
  An owner added without a later publish is invisible.
- **Account package lists are today's**, from `/-/user/<u>/package`. That endpoint answered 429 for
  21 of 103 accounts, including every control, so those lists come from the registry search
  `maintainer:<u>`, which undercounts (sindresorhus: 1,068 versus 1,287). Two accounts were sampled to
  1,500 packages (types, microsoft1es). False-alarm counts are therefore lower bounds.
- **Exposure repos were selected** by GitHub code search for `chalk-5.6.1.tgz` in a lockfile. All five
  commits are from 2025-09-08/09, so their lockfiles contain the bad versions. This inflates the
  version-level hits, not the package-level comparison. No project in either org uses a
  Shai-Hulud package, so the Shai-Hulud H1 numbers are package-level only.
- **Controls** came to 11 accounts, not 16. The four named accounts were already in the top 10, and
  @babel/core's last release was published by "GitHub Actions" (already a control).

## Deviations from the pre-registration

1. **H2 incident warning, clarified.** A firing counts for an incident only when its window
   contains the publish of one of the account's bad versions. The first run, without that check,
   credited routine bursts months earlier, for example scttcper in 2018. The control false-alarm
   counting is unchanged.
2. **The "excluding all bots" false-alarm rate** is extra and descriptive (not pre-registered).
3. **Recording windows** were narrowed to 2018-08..2018-12 and 2025-05-15..2025-12-31, plus the
   last version before each, to keep the dataset at 11 MB. Every query time lies inside them.
4. **The account-list fallback** to registry search (above) was not planned; it was forced by rate
   limiting.

## Reproduce

- `npm run proof:account` (offline) writes `test/replay/out/account-proof.md` and `.json`.
- Re-recording needs the network: `npx tsx test/replay/account/record-account.ts --osv-dir <OSV npm export> --cache <dir>`.
- Data and provenance live in `test/replay/account/data/` (`manifest.json`).

# Account-level proof (recorded real events, replayed offline)

Pre-registered in `test/replay/account/PREREGISTRATION.md` before any number below was computed.

Data: 10622 package timelines, 1200 OSV advisory entries, 103 accounts (see data/manifest.json).

## Verdicts (pre-registered rules)

| Hypothesis | Scope | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | chalk-debug-2025 | pass | 19 vs 1 bad packages named at T0; median gain 2.7 h; org exposures 204 vs 21 |
| H1 | event-stream-2018 | **fail** | 2 vs 2 bad packages named at T0; median gain 0 h; org exposures 2 vs 2 |
| H1 | shai-hulud-1 | **fail** | 37 bad packages named before their own advisory (accounts with ≥2 bad packages); median gain 0 h; precision 0.568 |
| H1 | shai-hulud-2 | pass | 245 bad packages named before their own advisory (accounts with ≥2 bad packages); median gain 1.3 h; precision 0.369 |
| H2 | N≥5, W=6h | **fail** | (a) qix lead 1.1 h: yes; (b) wave-1 accounts warned before T0 8/8: yes; (c) false alarms 2.095/account-month ≤ 0.1: no |
| H2-24h | N≥5, W=24h | **fail** | (a) qix lead 1.1 h: yes; (b) wave-1 accounts warned before T0 8/8: yes; (c) false alarms 1.991/account-month ≤ 0.1: no |

- Org exposures named at T0: **204** (bad packages: 204; would be named by advisories existing at T0: 21); median hours gained per bad exposure: **2.7**; precision (bad / named): 1.
